messages.author: 3a775dfa0a96bf95
messages.subject: Funny variable names in ggplot2
parts:
This works fine:

ggplot(data.frame(a=1:10,b=1:10)) + geom_line(aes(x=a,y=b))

This gives an error:

> ggplot(data.frame(`a b`=1:10,b=1:10)) + geom_line(aes(x=`a b`,y=b))
Error in eval(expr, envir, enclos) : object 'a ' not found

As far as I can tell, `a b` is a perfectly correct R identifier (name):

> class(quote(`a b`))
[1] "name"
> `a b` <- 234
> `a b`
[1] 234

Hi,

Try this,

ggplot(data.frame(`a b`=1:10,b=1:10)) + geom_line(aes(x=a.b,y=b))

ggplot(data.frame(`a b`=1:10,b=1:10, check.names = FALSE)) +
geom_line(aes(x=`a b`,y=b))

HTH,

baptiste

Ah, I see, sorry for the confusion -- this has nothing to do with ggplot, but is data.frame being overly helpful....

It turns out that my original problem didn't come from data.frame at all, but from sqlQuery, which does *not* perform check.names....

Sorry for the noise.
